items.title: 68087_Cliff Leeman oral history interview
items.q: when I went in with Eddie in '51... That was with Wild Bill -- Wild Bill Davison, Edmund Hall, Cutty Cutshall, Schroeder Gene Shrader

ctx.x: This is tape four of the Cliff Leeman story, and now Cliff Leeman will continue with his Condon story.

To get back to the Condon band, when I went in with Eddie in '51, that band was the most charging band, the most exciting -- I don't believe they ever had a bad night. I can't remember a bad night there. That was with Wild Bill -- Wild Bill Davison, Edmund Hall, Cutty Cutshall, Schroeder Gene Shrader -- Shrader Shroder -- take your pick.

I got Walter Page, I recommended Walter Page for the job, and Ralph Sutton, Lou McGerrity, and -- in those days, the place was jammed. I've seen them hang from the -- there was a railing around the top there, there was an upper part, and they'd come down from West Point, the Army-Navy games and so forth. And we played with that band, all the traditional Dixieland songs, because they were requested. They were references -- it was a Dixie style orchestra, which it was not. With Wild Bill and Eddie, and the manner…

items.title: 68087_Cliff Leeman oral history interview
items.q: We had Peanuts Hucko, Jack Lesberg, Gene Shrader, and Cutty Cutshall among others.

ctx.x: He continued his studies on drums, and along the way, after he went with Louis Armstrong -- he went all over the world with Louie Armstrong, and was such an outstanding soloist, and to this day, he's such a beautiful man, and he's still in the picture, I don't dare estimate what his age is -- I know it's around 70, and he's all over the world with Cootie Williams' orchestra, a small group, and they cover concerts all over the world, and they do some of the nicest work, and Cozy is still in there pitching. He is…

I must mention -- I did the first year of the Newport Festivals were starting, with Eddie Condon, for George Wein, Schroeder he was the promoter. We had Peanuts Hucko, Jack Lesberg, Gene Shrader, and Cutty Cutshall among others. And it rained

and it poured, and this great outdoor auditorium, and if you know anything about Eddie Condon, instead of playing the guitar, he took it upon himself to conduct the six pieces, and because of the rain which didn't cover the back, or the front of the show, where he announced, he had an umbrella over his head -- and it made quite a picture.
